subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acme.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Lina / Tom 

Thanks again for taking the time today 

 great conversation and really helpful context on your latency SLOs and the customer-critical hallucination cases. To recap the immediate ask: you want a short, reproducible eval against 1) the 150 proprietary prompts you shared (promptset v1) and 2) a latency profile that matches your peak-of-day traffic (p95 target <= 300ms for single-turn chats).

Per our discussion, attached is a compact shortlist of model variants I recommend we evaluate first, with quick rationale below. I included a one-page benchmark summary (pdf) with cost/latency ballpark numbers based on similar workloads.

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs are cost / median latency / quality notes):

- redwood/opt-6.7b-qlora (quantized):: low cost / 120-180ms median / strong instruction-following on short prompts; good for throughput-heavy flows but watch for drop in long-form factual recall.
- open/llama-2-13b-chat-8bit:: mid cost / 200-300ms median / better factuality and chat coherence for multi-turn; higher token cost but fewer hallucinations on our evals.
- redwood-instruct-3b-int8:: very low cost / 80-140ms median / excellent for simple classification/resolution tasks (80%+ accuracy in our internal NLU bench) but weaker on complex synthesis.
- fallback: open/llama-2-70b-chat (cpu/gpu mix):: high cost / 500ms+ median / best quality; use only for highest-risk flows or failover.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood runs a 3-day eval against your promptset v1 (we'll produce per-prompt quality metrics: exact-match where applicable, factuality flags, hallucination examples, and latency distribution).
- We'll return a short report and recommended production config (quantization, batching, KV cache settings) and a cost estimate for Hosted vs Dedicated options.
- If results look good, we can set up a short pilot on Dedicated for a week to validate SLAs.

Attachments: acme_eval_promptset_v1.csv (the prompts you shared) and redwood_acme_benchmark_summary_20260714.pdf (high-level cost/latency comps).

Questions for you: can you confirm the subset of prompts we should prioritize for the initial run (e.g., customer support FAQs vs long-form policy synthesis), and do you have any NDA/PO constraints for running sample data?

I'll loop in Rishi to coordinate the eval execution; he can trigger infra and provide the HubSpot/Drive links.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Marissa 

Thanks for the crisp recap and shortlist. Quick clarifying q's before we greenlight the eval:  
1) On hallucination rates 


 do you have an expected false/factuality flag rate for the opt-6.7b-qlora vs the 13b chat on tasks similar to our prompts? Rough percent ballpark would help us.
2) For the 300ms p95 target, are the median latencies you listed for single-token generation or full response times? Our production responses average ~120 tokens per turn.
3) Pricing: can you share an estimated cost per 1k tokens for each recommended variant (hosted) so we can model spend?

We are fine with Redwood using sample production data for the eval under the existing NDA, but I need confirmation that examples and logs will be scrubbed and that we can request deletion after the pilot. Also, prioritization: please start with 40 customer-support FAQ prompts (short), then 60 medium synthesis prompts (policy-related), and 50 long-form synthesis (>=200 tokens).

Thanks 

Lina Torres
Head of AI + Automation | Acme Corporation
lina.torres@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Lina 
 thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers inline and a proposed plan.

1) Hallucination/factuality (ballpark on our internal evals vs similar prompt classes):
   - redwood/opt-6.7b-qlora: ~8-12% factuality flags on medium/long prompts (we see more for >150 token generation).
   - open/llama-2-13b-chat-8bit: ~4-7% factuality flags on same prompt mix (better contextual reasoning).
   - redwood-instruct-3b-int8: ~10-15% on synthesis; strong on classification.
   Note: we always return example hallucination snippets in the evaluation report so you can decide risk tolerance per flow.

2) Latency numbers I sent are median full-response medians for typical response sizes; for p95 estimates with 120-token responses we expect:
   - opt-6.7b-qlora: p95 ~260-320ms (with 16-token KV warm cache and batching tuned for production).
   - llama-2-13b-chat-8bit: p95 ~320-400ms.
   - instruct-3b-int8: p95 ~180-240ms.

3) Ballpark hosted pricing (per 1k prompt+1k completion tokens) 
 - approximate, final pricing on contract:
   - opt-6.7b-qlora: $0.10 / 1k tokens
   - llama-2-13b-chat-8bit: $0.28 / 1k tokens
   - instruct-3b-int8: $0.06 / 1k tokens
   - llama-2-70b-chat (fallback): $1.20 / 1k tokens

Data handling: confirmed 
 - logs and examples used for the eval will be scrubbed of PII per the NDA and retained only for the duration of the eval. We will share a deletion confirmation after the run. If you prefer, we can run the eval on-site Dedicated (VPC) as an extra step to avoid any data leaving your environment.

Proposed immediate plan:
- Redwood runs a 3-day automated eval against the prioritized prompt subsets you provided (40/60/50).
- Deliverables: per-prompt QA table, example hallucination snippets, latency distributions, and a recommended production config + cost delta table (hosted vs dedicated).
- Timeline: start Thursday 16 Jul 2026 AM PT; report by Monday 20 Jul 2026 EOD.

Rishi 

 - can you confirm infra availability for Thursday and whether we need any short-lived credentials from Acme to run the prioritized prompts in-scope?

Thanks,
Marissa
